newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas to keep Japanese capacity.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas to keep Japanese capacity.

text.p: The International Air Services Commission (IASC) said on Monday it would renew Qantas Airways Ltd's application for capacity on its route to Japan.
"The commission did not believe it had grounds on which to conclude that Qantas had not served the route effectively," IASC chairman Jim Bain said in a statement.
"Accordingly, the commission is proposing to renew the determination in favour of Qantas, effective from 1 July 1997, subject to any submissions it may receive on the draft determination."
The decision to renew the agreement, which was due to expire on June 30 next year, means rival Ansett Australia has failed in its application for some of Qantas' capacity on that route.

"As this route is no longer in the start-up phase, the commission was required ... to assess whether Qantas had failed to service the route effectively before it could consider Ansett's requests for capacity," Bain said.
Ansett is owned equally by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd.
Bain said the commission had also issued a final determination in relation to the uncontested renewal of 1992 determinations allowing capacity to Qantas to Korea.
